text:
2026-07-29:
  [Politics and elections] Pope Leo XIV consecrates Fr. Francis Xavier Duan Yongkun as the coadjutor bishop of Bameng in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region under the 2018 provisional framework that cedes authority over its bishops to the Chinese government. ((Vatican News))
  [Politics and elections] The government of Nauru announces the official change of name of the country from Nauru to Naoero. ((RNZ))
  [Law and crime] Bolivian prosecutors issue an arrest warrant for former president Evo Morales for allegedly organizing protests and roadblocks across the country in May and June. The investigation follows complaints alleging armed uprising and terrorism. ((AFP via Firstpost))
  [Law and crime] Russia's Federal Security Service ​issues an arrest warrant on Telegram founder Pavel Durov for facilitating terrorist activity, alleging that Telegram helps Ukraine plan attacks in Russia. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Israeli forces strike a mosque in Gaza City in violation of the ongoing ceasefire and accuses Hamas of using it to store weapons. ((The New York Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Israeli forces accuse Hezbollah of launching a drone attack on its forces in the Ali al-Taher ridge of southern Lebanon, in violation of the ceasefire. ((AFP via Arab News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Israeli forces also claim that their 401st Brigade Combat Team and Yahalom Unit have destroyed an underground headquarters belonging to Hezbollah, located near a UNIFIL post. ((Israel National News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Saudi Arabian Armed Forces and United States Central Command (U.S. CENTCOM) launch strikes against Iran–backed militias in Iraq in response to Iranian drone attacks against oil facilities in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. ((Iraqi News)) ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Popular Mobilization Forces reports that 20 militants have been killed in joint Saudi–U.S. strikes. ((The Defense Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Several members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps are also confirmed to have been killed in the Saudi–U.S. strikes in Iraq. ((The New Region))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A drone strike targets the LNG storage tanker Energos Winter, which is leased by the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company, at the port of Damietta, Egypt. Additionally, another vessel is also targeted. The group responsible for the strike is currently unknown. ((The New York Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran in retaliation of a attempted attack by Iran against Jordan. ((AP))
  [Disasters and accidents] Two firefighters are killed while battling a wildfire near Rethymno, Crete, Greece, while a third dies near Gytheio, Laconia, during a separate operation. ((AFP via Malay Mail))
  [Disasters and accidents] A Bell 412 helicopter crashes while on a fire-fighting training operation in San Juan, Argentina, killing all seven occupants. ((AFP via NDTV))
  [Health and environment] Kenya Wildlife Service says preliminary tests indicated cyanide-contaminated tomatoes may have killed 15 elephants near Amboseli National Park over the past month, warning that livestock grazing in the area could also be exposed. ((AFP via The Manila Times))
2026-07-30:
  [Politics and elections] Argentine president Javier Milei issues a decree seeking parliamentary approval to bar or expel foreigners accused of inciting hatred against Argentina or its people, while exempting protected political, academic, and ideological expression. ((AFP via Vanguard))
  [Business and economy] The Intergovernmental Authority on Development trade bloc reopens its office in Khartoum, Sudan, resuming operations for the first time since the start of the country's civil war in April 2023. ((Sudan Horizon)) ((Sudan Tribune))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Pakistan foreign ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi reaffirms that talks between Iran and the United States are still ongoing despite recent strikes by the U.S. military. ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Jordanian air defenses shoot down five missiles from Iran. ((AP))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Kuwaiti authorities confirm that an Iranian attack targeted a building belonging to a Chinese company and killed one person. ((AFP via The Times of Israel)) ((Kuwait Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Egyptian cabinet confirms a drone has hit two vessels yesterday at a port in Damietta, Egypt, including the LNG storage tanker Energos Winter. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Data shows that the QatarEnergy-controlled LNG tanker Al Areesh exited the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the first LNG vessel from Qatar visible on ship-tracking data to do so since July 11, when Al Hamra exited the strait from Das Island, United Arab Emirates. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Mediators and Hamas reach an agreement to implement the second phase of a United States-backed ceasefire signed in October last year during a meeting in Cairo, Egypt. ((Egyptian Gazette))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Board of Peace has reached a deal for a complete disarmament of Hamas. ((BBC News)) ((Jewish Insider))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Amidst reports of a new plan to disarm Hamas, Israel reaffirms that it will not withdraw from the Gaza Strip, including the Yellow Line, until the militant organization is completely disarmed. ((The Jerusalem Post))
  [Disasters and accidents] The casualty toll from the earthquake in Kumamoto on Kyushu, Japan, earlier this week rises to 35 people killed and over 134 injured. ((Reuters))
  [Disasters and accidents] At least 34 miners are killed and more are reported missing after a methane gas explosion at a coal mine near Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan. ((AFP via Arab News))
  [Disasters and accidents] At least nine people are killed and several others are trapped after an explosion at a four-story building in Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, India. ((Hindustan Times))
  [Disasters and accidents] Five people are critically injured and six are missing after a residential building collapses during a gas leak explosion in Messina, Sicily, Italy. ((SkyNews24))
  [Disasters and accidents] Ten climbers are reported missing, including Nepalese mountaineer Nirmal Purja, after an avalanche on the Broad Peak in Pakistan. ((CNN)) ((The Indian Express))
  [Health and environment] The death toll from the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo rises to over 1,500 people killed. ((AP))
  [Health and environment] Singapore-based Hilleman Laboratories announces plans to advance an rVSV-based vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola into human trials after World Health Organization experts identified it as the most promising candidate for the epidemic. ((AFP via CNA))
  [Health and environment] The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports that the U.S. state has surpassed 10,000 cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. ((CBS News MI))
  [Health and environment] The Paks nuclear power plant in Hungary shuts down for the first time in 44 years amid a drought across the country and extremely low water levels on the Danube river. ((BBC News)) ((DW))
  [International relations] Thousands of undocumented immigrants cross into the Spanish autonomous city of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco. The city's mayor-president, Juan Jesús Vivas, requests the Spanish government to declare a national emergency, but is refused by the interior ministry. ((AP))
  [International relations] Senior Italian politicians, including prime minister Giorgia Meloni, deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini, and foreign minister Antonio Tajani, call for Spain to be kicked out of the Schengen Zone or the suspension of the Schengen Agreement entirely, citing the alleged threat of undocumented immigrants spreading throughout the European Union. ((Politico EU))
  [International relations] Chile and Venezuela restore diplomatic relations after a two-year suspension following Chile's call for a review of the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election results. ((AFP via The Manila Times))
  [International relations] Naoero announces it has withdrawn its recognition of Georgia's breakaway states Abkhazia and South Ossetia, terminating diplomatic relations with these entities "with immediate effect". ((Civil Georgia))
2026-07-31:
  [Politics and elections] The Bulgarian National Assembly sets 25 October as the date for the presidential election. ((AP))
  [Business and economy] South Korea's KOSPI index rises by 18%, its largest single-day gain in history, amid a surge of investment in AI. ((The New York Times))
  [Law and crime] Pakistani entrepreneur and Wafflix founder Mir Raza Ali Khan is found shot dead in Karachi, Pakistan, two days after he went missing. Police launch a murder investigation into the case. ((The Express Tribune))
  [Law and crime] A Sri Lankan court sentences former police chief Pujith Jayasundara to death for negligence in failing to prevent the 2019 Easter bombings, which killed 279 people. Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976. ((AFP via The Star))
  [Law and crime] Indonesian authorities announces it arrested a Malaysia Airlines pilot for allegedly smuggling over of ecstasy and a package of methamphetamine into Jakarta's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport. ((AP))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that it struck two tankers trying to pass the Strait of Hormuz with aerial protection from the United States, and forced four others to turn around. ((The Guardian))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Recent evidence by The New York Times show that a U.S. strike yesterday on Qeshm Island hit a family home and killed three people. ((The New York Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] At least eleven Palestinians, including four children, are injured during a raid by Israeli settlers and soldiers in Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers also detain at least ten people from Bethlehem, Nablus, Salim, and Tell. ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) confirms that they have killed a Mujahideen Brigades militant who was involved in the abduction of Avinatan Or and Noa Argamani during the Nova music festival massacre, and directing the abduction of Sudthisak Rinthalak during the October 7 attacks. ((The Jerusalem Post)) ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Hamas says that they will disarm if Israel withdraws from and ends its military campaign in the Gaza Strip and if Israel and the U.S. honors the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025. ((Middle East Eye)) ((The Washington Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The IDF says that killed two Hamas operatives accused of smuggling weapons into the Gaza Strip in separate strikes. ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Two warehouses in Volgograd and Zelenodolsk, Tatarstan, are attacked and set on fire, causing damage estimated at US$1.5 billion, in the latest of a series of Ukrainian drone strikes targeting Russian online retailer Wildberries. ((AFP via France 24)) ((Kyiv Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A migrant worker is fatally shot and another is injured by insurgents in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. ((The Indian Express))
  [Disasters and accidents] A bus en route to Algiers, Algeria, plunges into a deep ravine in El Kerma after skidding off the road, killing 25 people and injuring 44 others. ((AP))
  [Disasters and accidents] Twelve people, including five children, are killed and 66 others are injured after a bus overturns on the N1 highway near Trompsburg, Free State, South Africa. ((IOL))
  [Disasters and accidents] Two bodies and a body part are recovered after an avalanche on the Broad Peak in Pakistan buried ten climbers yesterday, including Nirmal Purja, who remains missing. ((BBC News))
  [Health and environment] A cancer patient at the Christie hospital in Manchester, United Kingdom, becomes the first to receive the ZI-MA4-1 therapy. ((BBC)) ((The Independent))
  [International relations] Ceutan mayor-president Juan Jesús Vivas says that around 60,000 undocumented migrants have entered the Spanish exclave in North Africa in the last 24 hours, as the death toll rises to 57. ((The Guardian)) ((BBC News))
  [International relations] Videos on social media appear to show the Spanish Army deploying military vehicles towards the border with Morocco. ((Reuters))
  [International relations] French interior minister Laurent Nuñez announces that he has ordered increased controls at the border with Spain amid fears the thousands of migrants entering Ceuta could make their way to France. ((Politico))
  [International relations] Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker and Finnish interior minister Mari Rantanen join Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni in calling for Spain to be suspended from the Schengen Area in response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta over the last 24 hours. ((AA))
  [International relations] Spanish authorities close the Melilla border crossing with Morocco after around 400 migrants stormed the border barrier. RTVE reports the sound of gunfire and explosions. ((AA))
  [International relations] Italy suspends Schengen border-free travel with Spain, introducing checks on air and sea passengers and strengthening controls with France along the France–Italy border. ((Reuters))
  [International relations] Spain's interior ministry says authorities have returned about 48,300 of roughly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco. ((CBS News))
  [International relations] Latvia announces the sudden closure of its border with Belarus, citing "technical reasons". ((Reuters))
2026-08-01:
  [Law and crime] Four people are killed, including the perpetrator, and seven others are injured in a mass shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, United States. ((CNN)) ((Reuters))
  [Law and crime] The U.S. FBI opens an investigation after the U.S. state of Michigan reports a cyberattack on its water systems, including whether Iran was behind the cyberattack, a day after Minnesota reported a similar breach. ((Al Jazeera)) ((ABC News))
  [Law and crime] Four workers are killed in a mass shooting in Nyanga, Western Cape, South Africa, while they were repairing a flat tyre. ((The Witness))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Bermuda-flagged LNG tanker Gaslog Shanghai, which was carrying LNG oil from Qatar, is reported to have been among the two vessels hit yesterday in the Strait of Hormuz. ((Arab Times Kuwait)) ((Bloomberg))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A tanker near Oman is hit by an unknown projectile. ((CNBC))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that its military has detected and intercepted Iranian drones entering the country's airspace. ((Kuwait Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] United States embassies in the Middle East warn Americans to depart the region amidst fears of a potential escalation in the war. ((AFP via Arab News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] U.S. president Donald Trump cancels a planned attack against Iran, citing progress in ceasefire negotiations. ((Axios)) ((The Japan Times))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Israeli airstrikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza City, bringing the total casualties in the past 24 hours to seven. ((Al-Ahram)) ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A Board of Peace official reports that Hamas will disarm its weapons in the coming days. ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Israeli military says it has killed several Hezbollah fighters in an Israeli-held area of southern Lebanon, despite a ceasefire framework between Israel and Lebanon. ((AFP via South China Morning Post))
  [Disasters and accidents] The Old Trails wildfire in northwestern Spokane, Washington, United States, burns over , destroying many structures. Residents near Fort Spokane are told to evacuate. ((CNN)) ((News.az))
  [Disasters and accidents] Cuba reports a partial collapse of the national power grid, leaving western provinces without electricity after transmission lines fail between Matanzas and Pinar del Río. ((Xinhua))
  [Disasters and accidents] Thirteen people, including eleven tourists, are killed when a small aircraft crashes near the Nazca Lines, Peru, after departing Pisco, Ica. ((Firstpost))
  [Disasters and accidents] All ten climbers, including Nirmal Purja, are confirmed deceased after an avalanche at Broad Peak in Pakistan on July 30. ((Al Jazeera))
  [Health and environment] Protesters block parts of the main highway connecting Port Sudan and Khartoum in Suakin and Jubayt over severe power cuts amidst a heat wave reported by the Sudan Meteorological Authority in Red Sea State, Sudan. ((Sudan Tribune))
  [International relations] Moroccan security forces clash with hundreds of migrants as they attempt to storm the Spanish enclave of Melilla. Several Moroccan security personnel are reportedly injured while more than 50 migrants are detained. ((Yeni Safak))
2026-08-02:
  [Politics and elections] Incumbent Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva formally announces his candidacy for a fourth term as the Workers' Party's nominee in October’s presidential election. ((AFP via France 24))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Iranian lawmaker Hassan Ghashghavi says that efforts to restore the Islamabad Memorandum deal between Iran and the United States are underway. ((AFP via Arab News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says that Iran and Oman are nearing a deal to manage the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. halted its recent strikes against the country. ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) confirm that they killed three militants in separate strikes last week, including a Jaish al-Islam militant in Gaza City, a Hamas commander in the Jabalya Battalion, and a Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant. ((The Jerusalem Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The IDF's 401st Brigade says that they have destroyed 1,200 Hezbollah tunnels and concluded their mission in southern Lebanon, ending their eight-month deployment. ((Israel National News)) ((The Jerusalem Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] New clashes are reported across the Tigray Region in northern Ethiopia between the Ethiopian federal army and Tigray People's Liberation Front, four years after the previous war in the region ended, prompting hundreds to flee to war-torn Sudan amidst fears of a new civil war. ((BBC)) ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Several Ethiopian refugees are reportedly killed after projectiles have hit refugee camps across the Ethiopia–Sudan border. ((Sudan Tribune))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A drone strike hits a customary court in Kabkabiya District, North Darfur, Sudan, killing at least 37 people. ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Police say a suspected suicide bombing outside a police station in Kabal, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killed at least 17 people, including seven officers and the suspected bomber, and injured at least 34 others. ((Reuters))
  [Disasters and accidents] Two people are killed when two firefighting helicopters collide near Athens, Greece. ((BBC News))
  [Disasters and accidents] Spanish officials say at least 72 people died during the mass migrant crossing from Morocco into the autonomous city of Ceuta. ((Reuters))
  [Disasters and accidents] Six people are killed and 27 more injured in a traffic collision between a bus, a camper, and three cars in Colli sul Velino, Province of Rieti, Italy. ((Xinhua))
  [Disasters and accidents] A ferry catches fire off the coast of Madura, Indonesia, leaving at least five people dead and 41 others missing. ((BBC News))
  [Health and environment] South Korea's weather agency records in Yangsan, South Gyeongsang, the country's highest temperature since observations began. ((AFP via France 24))
  [International relations] The Dominican Republic and Venezuela agree on a framework to gradually restore diplomatic relations, which deteriorated after the Dominican Republic questioned the results of the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election. ((AFP via Jamaica Observer))
2026-08-03:
  [Politics and elections] Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin, who attempted to contest the 2024 presidential election on a platform against the Russo-Ukrainian war, announces that he has fled the country to France following growing pressure on him and his family. ((The Moscow Times))
  [Law and crime] The Polish health ministry appeals a Brussels court ruling that ordered the country to accept and pay approximately €1.3 billion for unwanted COVID-19 vaccine doses produced by Pfizer and BioNTech. ((Politico EU))
  [Law and crime] South African news outlets report that over 170 people have been murdered in the Western Cape, South Africa in the past 2 weeks. ((Independent Online))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A Board of Peace envoy meets Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and urges a halt in strikes across the Gaza Strip. However, they also announce that Israel will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas completely disarms. ((The New Region)) ((The Washington Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reports that dozens of children and civilians have been killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend, violating the ongoing ceasefire. ((Xinhua))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Two Palestinian civilians are killed in an Israeli missile strike near a mosque which targeted a civilian vehicle southwest of Gaza City. ((Middle East Eye))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) claim that they have killed Palestinian Islamic Jihad commander Mahmoud Fatair, who took part in the abduction of Rom Braslavski, in the Deir al-Balah area of the Gaza Strip during the Nova music festival massacre on October 7, 2023. ((The Jerusalem Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The IDF claim that they have killed two Hamas militants in separate airstrikes in central Gaza and the Shati camp in Gaza City respectively, violating the ongoing ceasefire. ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Shipping data shows that two tanker ships carrying oil from Saudi Arabia, the Suezmax Malta-flagged Lesvos and the VLCC Desh Vaibhav, have exited the Red Sea through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] At least seven people, including three children, are killed and 40 others are injured when drone debris falls on a crowded beach in Gelendzhik, Krasnodar Krai, Russia. ((CNN))
  [Disasters and accidents] The death toll from the two earthquakes that hit Venezuela in June exceeds 6,000 people according to figures from lawmaker Jorge Rodríguez. ((Reuters))
  [Disasters and accidents] At least fourteen people are killed in a series of floods in southern India. ((Reuters))
  [Disasters and accidents] Guatemala's disaster agency declares a nationwide orange alert following a major eruption of Fuego volcano and begins evacuating two nearby villages. ((AFP via RNZ))
  [Health and environment] Scotland's NatureScot denies a 2026 licence for hunting northern gannets on Sula Sgeir, citing possible harm to the local gannet population after recent bird-flu deaths. ((AFP via RFI))
  [Health and environment] Italy experiences its fourth heatwave of the summer with the health ministry issuing red alerts for a record 25 cities. ((AA))
  [Health and environment] Michigan, U.S., reports the first two deaths of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by cyclospora cayetanensis. ((AP))
2026-08-04:
  [Law and crime] The Colombian Special Jurisdiction for Peace charges 27 former FARC members, including ex-commander Timoleón Jiménez, with crimes against humanity and sexual violence committed during the conflict, including killings, disappearances, displacement, and rape. ((AFP via The Manila Times))
  [Law and crime] Kyrgyz president Sadyr Japarov signs a law banning the use of cremation for deceased human bodies in Kyrgyzstan. ((AKIPress)) ((Kabar))
  [Law and crime] South Sudanese police arrest 60 suspected gang members in a series of operations targeting criminal gangs, drug trafficking and youth delinquency in Juba. ((Sudans Post))
  [Law and crime] Four people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting spree by a rogue Russian soldier in Sevastopol, Russian-occupied Crimea. ((CBS News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Mediators from Qatar reports that progress has been made in efforts to end the war between the United States and Iran. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Liberian-flagged bulk carrier Minoan Pioneer is reported to be missing in the Strait of Hormuz after it was struck by a unknown projectile northeast of Oman. ((Seatrade Maritime News)) ((Al Arabiya)) ((Haaretz))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Shipping data from Kpler reports that Iraq has exported over 30 million barrels of crude oil through the strait between July 4 and August 4. ((Asharq Al-Awsat))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] It is reported that the United States Army has used most of its ATACMS and Precision Strike missiles during the war in Iran including Operation Epic Fury. ((Military Times)) ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] A mass funeral is held for 112 bodies that were recovered from a Israeli strike in the Sabra neighborhood of Gaza City during the early weeks of the war. ((Haaretz))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Yemen's internationally recognized government says a projectile attack sank the Indian-flagged cargo ship MSV Faize Noore Oliya in the Red Sea near the coast of Hodeidah, with all 14 crew members rescued. ((AFP via Arab News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Rapid Support Forces senior commander and brigadier general Mahdi Adam Ismail, also known as Jebel Moon, is confirmed to be killed during clashes with the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Joint Forces in West Darfur, Sudan. His death is confirmed by Sudan Liberation Movement leader and Darfur governor Minni Arko Minnawi. ((Sudan Tribune)) ((Sudan Nabaa))
  [Health and environment] Health Canada announces it has given Moderna the green light for authorization to launch a clinical trial for a mRNA Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo strain of the ebolavirus. ((CBC))
  [Health and environment] Austria records in Vienna, the highest temperature in the country's history, as a heat wave also brings wildfires and historically low Danube water levels. ((Xinhua))
  [Health and environment] The Bradley Creek fire in North Okanagan, British Columbia, Canada destroys 250 homes on the North Okanagan Indian reservation in a night with 150km/h winds.((Global News))
  [International relations] The United States revokes the visa of Brazilian ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti to reciprocate Brazil's denial of visas to two U.S. diplomats. The State Department says the action does not expel Viotti from the country. ((AFP via New Straits Times))
2026-08-05:
  [Politics and elections] Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina announces that she plans to return to the country from exile in New Delhi, India, despite facing a death sentence for her role during a violent crackdown on protesters that led to her resignation two years ago. ((Sky News))
  [Law and crime] Sindh Police detain 19 people for questioning as part of the investigation into the murder of Karachi entrepreneur and Wafflix founder Mir Raza Ali. ((Daily Pakistan)) ((ARY News))
  [Law and crime] The Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, convicts seven members and one supporter of a right-wing extremist group called Last Defense Wave and sentences them to prison for attempted murder, arson, aggravated assault, and being members of a terrorist organisation for planning and carrying out arson and bomb attacks on asylum seeker shelters. ((AP))
  [Law and crime] The Spanish Civil Guard and the Ecuadorian National Police announce they have arrested 44 people and confiscated 21 tons of cocaine as part of a multiyear investigation on a drug trafficking ring financed by investors in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. ((AP))
  [Law and crime] A drone loaded with explosives is found and defused at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany, while a cargo Boeing 757 had a collision with another supposed UAV at the same airport. ((Reuters)) ((DW))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Iran and Oman reach an agreement understanding on geographic coordinates for shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz. ((Reuters)) ((Euronews))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Talks between Israel and Lebanon are on pause following alleged leaks and will resume tomorrow. ((Al-Monitor))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says they have launched strikes in southern Lebanon after alleged ceasefire violations by Hezbollah. ((The Times of Israel))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Two Israeli soldiers are killed in action and four others are wounded in an improvised explosive device bombing in Majdal Zoun, South Governorate, Lebanon. ((Anadolu Ajansı))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] IDF chief Eyal Zamir visits the Gaza Strip to conduct an assessment in the enclave. He also states that the military will continue to operate proactively. ((The Jerusalem Post))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Russian forces launch dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, Ukraine, killing at least 17 people, including eight civilians at a railway station in Kyiv Oblast, and wounding dozens more. None of the missiles were intercepted by Ukrainian forces due to a shortage of Patriot missiles, according to president Volodymyr Zelenskyy. ((The Guardian))
  [Disasters and accidents] Five people are killed after two vehicles collided head-on and burst into flames on the Stuart Highway, Australia. ((Xinhua))
  [Health and environment] The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves Moderna's mRNA influenza vaccine for people aged 50 and older. ((Time)) ((Reuters))
  [International relations] The United States Treasury Department lifts sanctions against Fly Baghdad, which were previously imposed in 2024 over its links to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force. ((Al-Monitor)) ((Reuters))
  [International relations] The Holy See Press Office announces Pope Leo XIV will make an apostolic journey to Argentina, Uruguay, and his home country of Peru, in November, marking his first trip to Latin America in his papacy. ((AP)) ((Holy See))
2026-08-06:
  [Business and economy] The Competition and Markets Authority of the United Kingdom clears Paramount Skydance's US$110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, while culture secretary Lisa Nandy declines a public-interest review after receiving commitments on editorial independence. ((AA))
  [Law and crime] Former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre Rivero is arrested on charges of forced disappearance and obstruction of justice. He is accused of ordering the concealment of security camera footage that showed police intercepting a bus carrying students in Iguala in 2014, who have never been found. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Ugandan authorities approve a measure to send troops from Uganda to the Gaza Strip as part of the International Stabilization Force proposed by the Board of Peace to secure the enclave following the war. ((NBC News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Houthis announce a military offensive against Saudi-backed government forces in Marib Governorate and Hadhramaut Governorate, with over 30 soldiers being killed in two missile attacks. ((Al Jazeera))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Ukrainian forces launch drone attacks on two oil refineries in Russia, the Yaroslavl refinery and a Bashneft-Novoil refinery in Bashkortostan, causing large fires at the facilities. ((BBC News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Six people are killed in Russian airstrikes across Ukraine, including three civilians in Kharkiv Oblast, while a total power outage occurs in the city of Kherson after critical infrastructure was targeted overnight by Russian drones. ((Al Jazeera)) ((Antikor))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] It is reported that the situation on the border between Ethiopia and Sudan is calm following recent clashes between the Ethiopian Army and Tigray People's Liberation Front that sparked fears of a new conflict four years after a peace agreement was signed in 2022 to end the war in Tigray. ((Sudan Tribune))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti reports that 613 people were killed and 375 others injured between March 6 and July 31 amid intensifying gang violence across the country. ((Caribbean Broadcasting Corporation))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Two people are killed and 13 others are injured when an explosive device detonates on a passenger minibus in Jaramana, Syria. ((AA))
  [Disasters and accidents] Civil officials state that ten children passengers are reported missing after a wooden boat capsized on the Lulua River, Demba Territory, Kasai-Central, Democratic Republic of the Congo.((AA))
  [Disasters and accidents] Six people are killed and 19 others are injured after a bus crashed in Constantine Province, Algeria. ((Xinhua))
  [Health and environment] Congolese health authorities monitor passengers from a boat near Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, after a traveler died from Ebola complications. ((The Washington Post))
  [International relations] Ceuta mayor-president Juan Jesús Vivas confirms that at least 100 people died during last week's migrant surge into the Spanish autonomous city of Ceuta, while around 3,500 to 5,000 undocumented migrants remain in the city. ((Reuters))
2026-08-07:
  [Politics and elections] Abelardo de la Espriella is sworn in as the president of Colombia after winning the presidential election in June. ((AP))
  [Law and crime] A judge of the Karachi High Court in Pakistan allows the exhumation of Mir Raza Ali's body. ((Dawn))
  [Law and crime] Nine people are killed, including the shooter, and 15 others are injured in a shooting spree between a home and the Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Bang Kruai district, Nonthaburi province, Thailand. ((AP)) ((The Guardian))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Indian shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal reports that more than 4,000 seafarers from India have been repatriated and 62 Indian vessels have successfully transited through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. ((Lokmat Times)) ((India New England News))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company reports that 15 of its vessels have been attacked by missiles or drones while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz since the war with Iran started on February 28. ((Reuters))
  [Armed conflicts and attacks] Israeli forces withdraw from the Qalandiyah refugee camp and Kafr 'Aqab neighborhood in occupied West Bank following a two-day raid, with Palestinian Authority reporting 51 injuries. ((Haaretz))
